item.title: Post Mortem: axios NPM supply chain compromise
item.description:
Please reload this page. 0 published to npm March 31, 00:21 UTC: axios@1. 1 injected March 31, around 01:00 UTC: axios@0.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 5 Comments:

Zopieux:

Not much we didn't know (you're basically SOL since an owner was compromised), however we now have a small peek into the actual meat of the social engineering, which is the only interesting news imho: https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/10636#issuecomment-418...

akersten:

Any good payload analysis been published yet? Really curious if this was just a one and done info stealer or if it potentially could have clawed its way deeper into affected systems.

charcircuit:

Does OIDC flow block this same issue of being able to use a RAT to publish a malicious package?

fraywing:

Incredible uptick in supply chain attacks over the last few weeks.

I feel like npm specifically needs to up their game on SA of malicious code embedded in public projects.

uticus:

> March 31, around 01:00 UTC: community members file issues reporting the compromise. The attacker deletes them using the compromised account.

Interesting it got caught when it did.

item.title: A Few Good Magazines From the 70s and 80s
item.description:
BYTE is still worth reading, 50 years later. , Creative Computing and BYTE were listings. Even modems were somewhat rare.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 3 Comments:

watersb:

The article states that "Playboy" magazine creators started "Omni", but I'm almost certain it was "Penthouse".

I would describe both Playboy and Penthouse as primarily pornography. As such, they were both wildly popular in the 1970s and early 1980s.

Omni was not that. I had a subscription to Omni from the first issue in 1978 until about 1983. Pop science, science fiction, fantasy art, interviews and features on space exploration policy... and junk science, UFOs, psychic powers, cults. News of the wierd.

TuringNYC:

I thought of OMNI before anything and was pleased to find it on the article :-)

defrost:

Dr. Dobbs Journal of Computer Calisthenics and Orthodontia was my goto, I boot strapped my first C compiler from Ron Cain's Small-C code.

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small-C

* https://github.com/trcwm/smallc_v1

ParadeDB (YC S23) Is Hiring Database Internal Engineers (Rust)
Memo: A language that remembers only the last 12 lines of code
item.description:
[]memo is a stream-of-conscious coding environment. []memo is functional and uses natural-language syntax: List elements are seperated by commas, ands or both. []memo ignores numerals like 4 and expects four instead: Some values are approximated.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 3 Comments:

dcre:

How exciting, I get to be the pedant: it’s “stream-of-consciousness,” not “stream-of-conscious.” Conscious is an adjective; there can’t be a stream of it.

stitched2gethr:

This is intriguing.

On another note, I do not understand how posts make it to the top of the front page with essentially no comments.

dlcarrier:

In my country, we call that an interactive shell.

Fun fact, if you run Python from a command line, with no options, it defaults to such a shell.
